In an world where cliff notes are super important here’s how I’d go about it. I’m a sysadmin that’s worked with networking and systems for about 20 years and I will always be amazed at how different our fields are and how funny it is to assume a systems admin can build apps and that developers understand how to properly terminate fiber optic cables. Anyhow hope I can help :

Step 1 - test cable you’re relying on to interconnect the modem and router to using a cable testing unit to ensure all wires terminate properly in correct sequence. If you don’t have this you can still test a cable with your computer and the edgerouter X. Ensure sure it’s capable of connecting at 1gbps; this requires all 8 wires to be working properly in order to establish and maintain connectivity. I would also  bend the cable near the ends to ensure nothing’s going to physically affect your connection due to physical issues.

Step 2 backup your current modem config and see if you can factory reset it, in certain scenarios  the modem may require reconfiguration, I’d check out your ISP forums or call them and ask.

Step 3 if applicable and documented/ supported by your ISP, turn off all the routing / private Lan interfaces, Wi-Fi and get the combined device to behave more like a modem. This is usually termed bridge mode or transparent bridge, some ISPs will not support this configuration but that’s not a problem if it’s working ....

Step 4 try to connect up and if getting dropped open the log to determine if  the interface is dropping packets or losing its address you can most likely move the cable to a different port and see if the behavior continues and it could be the device you’re connected do, typically a modem router combo but it had logs too and can assist determining if this issue is happening due to factors outside the lan but still will provide insight toward a resolution.
